final_answer: The interaction effect size between baseline insulin resistance status and the protein-vs-fiber peak glucose reduction in the rice mitigator challenge was -0.90 glucose units (HC3 robust 95% CI: -8.94 to 7.14; p = 0.826) using SSPG median split to define insulin resistance. This is not statistically significant and provides no evidence of a meaningful interaction in the available sample.
final_text: Selected agent: `tabular_genomics_analyst`, because the task asks for a statistical interaction effect on already-assembled clinical/glycemic data rather than omics matrix modeling.
grader_notes: The agent mistakenly computed glucose nadir instead of peak, used Protein−Fiber instead of Fiber−Protein, omitted the required two-way ANOVA, and did not report partial eta-squared. IR classification failed to prioritize DI. These errors propagated to all subsequent steps, making the final answer substantially incorrect relative to the rubric expectations.

criterion_1.reason: Classified IR using only SSPG with median split; did not use DI as primary marker and did not fall back to SSPG for missing DI as required by rubric.

criterion_2.reason: Computed nadir (minimum post-meal glucose) instead of peak (maximum post-meal glucose) and derived a reduction metric from it, fundamentally misrepresenting peak glucose.

criterion_3.reason: Computed Protein minus Fiber difference instead of Fiber minus Protein, resulting in wrong sign and misinterpretation of the reduction direction.

criterion_4.reason: Tested the interaction using a linear model on difference scores rather than a two-way ANOVA with an explicit interaction term, and did not report the ANOVA F-statistic.

criterion_5.reason: Did not calculate partial eta-squared or any formal effect size measure; only reported the unstandardized coefficient and R-squared.

criterion_6.reason: Numerical results are traceable to provided files, but clinical interpretation references are unrelated (HOMA-IR paper) or missing; no real peer-reviewed citations for protein preload effects.
